headline: USAR BEGINS COMMERCIAL-SCALE HEAVY RARE EARTH SHIPMENTS — FIRST DOMESTIC US SALE TO GOVT PARTNER
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) announced November 9 that it has begun commercial-scale shipments and completed the first sale of heavy rare earth carbonate from its Round Top facility in Texas — a milestone that moves USAR from development to revenue-generating operations and delivers domestically sourced heavy rare earths to a government-funded offtake partner for the first time. The announcement follows the company's Q3 2026 earnings release and a Department of Energy funding win, with management citing material shortages as the principal near-term operational constraint.

headline: EQUINOX GOLD Q3: CALIBRE COMBINATION 'BEGINS TO DELIVER' — NINE-MINE PORTFOLIO RAMPS AT $4,100 GOLD
snippet: Equinox Gold (TSX/NYSE: EQX) reported Q3 2026 results showing its transformational merger with Calibre Mining is beginning to deliver the anticipated production scale and cost synergies, with the combined nine-mine Latin American and North American portfolio generating improved operational metrics at $4,100+ gold. The results position Equinox as a key mid-tier beneficiary of the structural gold bull market, with management's headline message — 'transformational combination begins to deliver' — reinforcing the case for the merger's long-term value creation thesis.

headline: GOLD REBOUNDS TO $4,125 AS DOLLAR WEAKENS, SILVER +2.6% TO $53.39 — CPI SELLOFF FULLY REVERSED
snippet: Spot gold recovered to approximately $4,125 on November 10, fully reversing Monday's CPI-triggered selloff to $4,080, as the US dollar index gave back gains and silver outperformed with a 2.6% surge to $53.39 — returning to levels last seen before the October CPI release. The recovery confirms the $4,000–$4,100 band as durable support, with the dollar's softening the primary driver rather than any shift in the Fed rate outlook; December's priced-in 81% hike probability remains intact.

headline: BARRICK DEEP DIVE: EPS UP 41% Y/Y, $270M EBITDA PER $100/oz GOLD — REKO DIQ AND IPO ARE NEXT CATALYSTS
snippet: Investing.com's post-earnings analysis of Barrick Mining (TSX/NYSE: ABX) puts the Q3 2026 beat in context: adjusted EPS of $0.82 (up 41% year-over-year) translates to $270 million in EBITDA leverage per $100/oz gold move at current prices, while the stock remains well below its 52-week high. The analysis identifies three next catalysts — Reko Diq copper production ramp in Balochistan, the pending North American Gold IPO S-1 filing this month, and Q4 guidance confirmation — that could drive a re-rating for the world's second-largest gold producer.

headline: ERAMET DUMPS ARIZARO LITHIUM ARGENTINA FOR $71M — SELLS NICKEL ASSETS TOO IN BALANCE SHEET RESET
snippet: French mining major Eramet is selling its undeveloped Arizaro lithium concessions in Argentina's Puna region for $71 million — with closing targeted before year-end — alongside nickel asset disposals as part of a balance sheet reset targeting debt reduction. The exit confirms that majors are shedding non-core lithium exposure at current depressed prices while keeping the structural supply gap intact; for TSX-V and ASX lithium developers, Eramet's willingness to transact at $71M on an undeveloped Argentine concession suggests a floor is forming in Lithium Triangle asset values despite Citi's recent 40% price forecast cut.

headline: STANDARD URANIUM UPSIZES LIFE OFFERING, TRANCHE 1 CLOSES TODAY — ATHABASCA BASIN DRILLING AHEAD
snippet: Standard Uranium (TSX-V: STND) further upsized its LIFE flow-through equity offering, with the first tranche scheduled to close November 10, 2026 and a second tranche on or about November 17 — proceeds fund exploration drilling across its Athabasca Basin uranium portfolio in Saskatchewan. The raise arrives as the Basin's south-rim exploration window enters the 2026–27 winter campaign season, with spot uranium near $91/lb providing sufficient incentive for drill-funded exploration in one of the world's most prospective uranium districts.

headline: TUNGSTEN BOOM OPENS DOORS FOR AUSSIE JUNIORS — CHINA'S 85% SUPPLY GRIP FUELS CRITICAL MINERAL PUSH
snippet: Stockhead identifies a broadening tungsten rally creating re-rating potential for Australian junior miners with critical mineral exposure, as China's control of approximately 85% of global tungsten supply drives industrial and defence buyers to seek non-Chinese alternatives. Flynn Gold's Firetower project in Queensland — hosting high-grade tungsten-gold mineralisation — is among the beneficiaries highlighted, with the dual commodity angle (tungsten critical mineral + gold bull market) creating a differentiated investment case for small-cap investors tracking both themes simultaneously.

headline: US1 CRITICAL MINERALS RESTRUCTURES TANZANIAN URANIUM DEAL — $1M PAYMENT SPLIT TO EASE CAPEX TIMING
snippet: ASX-listed US1 Critical Minerals (ASX: USC) amended its agreement with Bradda Head Lithium for the acquisition of the Mkuju, Foxy, and Eland uranium tenements in Tanzania, restructuring the US$1 million acquisition payment into two equal tranches of US$500,000 each to ease near-term capital deployment. The Tanzanian uranium assets sit in the same East African corridor where Lotus Resources' Malawi Kayelekera mine shipped its inaugural 145,000 lb concentrate last week — suggesting the broader East Africa uranium theme is developing material pipeline alongside Malawi's operating asset.

headline: RESOURCE TALKS: 4 JUNIOR MINERS TO WATCH — MANAGEMENT CONVERSATIONS AND UPCOMING CATALYSTS
snippet: Resource Talks' latest Substack dispatch rounds up conversations with four junior mining management teams from the past week, offering a ground-level read on how smaller companies are navigating the current market — including capital allocation priorities, upcoming drill catalysts, and how they're positioning for 2027 as $4,100+ gold amplifies project economics for gold developers while lithium and nickel teams continue to manage through depressed commodity cycles. These direct management-insight pieces complement analyst coverage for self-directed junior mining investors doing primary-source due diligence.
